topics.topic: Construction and concrete contents of the alternate class-policy test release
questions: How will the Factory construct the alternate release, and which concrete service, answer and field will its changed row use?
How does Factory verification construct and run the required test release with altered class-policy constants?
How is the alternate release with changed imported class constants constructed for Required tests 5 and 6?

quotes:
The check is made on every answer all the same, and it is shown
   on a test release whose class tables — the imported
   `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant and the imported
   `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1) — differ from the
   first release's in the one row a test gives (Required tests 5 and 6).

On a test release whose class tables give a service a highest class
   below a class one of its answers carries, that answer is refused whole:
   no field of it is disclosed (rule 4).
judgement.why: State 2 fixes the alternate-release outcomes and what tests 5 and 6 must demonstrate, while fixture construction and the particular qualifying answer field are Factory-check choices.
options: Generate a complete test-only data-provider fixture and assemble an alternate release from it.
Inject alternate constant tables while assembling the verification release.
Parameterize release generation from a Factory fixture.
consequences: A complete fixture exercises release assembly but adds fixture-generation work.
Injection is smaller but requires proof that production cannot select the replacement.
Parameterized generation is reusable but introduces a Factory-owned fixture interface.

topics.topic: Dedicated owner-interface host, DNS, TLS, and routing configuration
questions: Which host name, DNS or hosts-file mapping, TLS endpoint and service-routing arrangement will provide the isolated owner-interface host?
Which concrete host name, DNS mapping and certificate binding does the deployment assign exclusively to the owner interface?
Which dedicated host name, DNS or hosts-file mapping, TLS endpoint and routing arrangement provide the owner interface's isolated host name?

quotes:
The
   host name is a fact of the deployment, which Registry cannot check, as
   the addresses are (A17 rule 1): providing it and keeping every other
   HTTPS service of the host off it is a deployment step, carried to the
   deployment's owner (the Factory's platform deployment).
judgement.why: The required hostname isolation is decided, but choosing the concrete name, resolution, certificate endpoint and routing arrangement belongs to deployment.
options: Use a dedicated private DNS name with TLS terminated directly at Registry.
Use a dedicated private DNS name at a reverse proxy that routes only that name to Registry.
Use a dedicated VPN-local or hosts-file name with a locally managed certificate.
consequences: Direct termination minimizes routing components but makes Registry's deployment responsible for the certificate endpoint.
A reverse proxy centralizes TLS but must preserve exclusive routing for the hostname.
A VPN-local or hosts-file name avoids public DNS but increases client resolution and certificate administration.
judgement.requirement:
the deployment gives the owner interface a host name of its
   own, under which no other HTTPS service answers — on the home server not
   the kernel workplace, the gateway or PresuPro — and no other service of
   the same host receives the owner session cookie.

topics.topic: Factory method for creating and verifying the confirmation-time collision without prescribing hidden implementation seams or function names
questions: How will the Factory deterministically create the post-step collision and verify the transactional clean-mapping guard without making an accidental hidden function shape part of the contract?
Must Factory verification demonstrate the collision branch by executable random-source replacement, by a structural code gate, or by both?
How does the Factory replace or control the random source to create the post-step identifier collision without fixing a hidden production implementation seam in State 2?
Must generation expose a symbol literally named `confirm_import`, or may the Factory verify the required transactional behavior independently of generated function names?

quotes:
A confirmation applies the mapping of the file and the picks it is bound
   to (rule 2, A13 rule 6), which it builds once, from the kept bytes,
   inside the confirming transaction, as it must to write the records; it
   applies that mapping only when it is clean, and otherwise refuses the
   whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).

Through Registry's surfaces alone a minted id cannot be chosen, so the
    refusal is checked on the code by the Factory — `confirm_import`
    builds the mapping inside the confirming transaction and applies it

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
